data.name: Mujawir

in_arabic.name: مُجَوّٖر
in_arabic.meaning: المُجَوّٖرُ: الَّذي يُجَوَّرُ في المُجاوَرَةِ، المُجاوِرُ، المُجاوَرَةُ
in_arabic.long_meaning: المُجَوّٖرُ: الَّذي يُجَوَّرُ في المُجاوَرَةِ، المُجاوِرُ، المُجاوَرَةُ. يُشير الاسم إلى الشخص الذي حصل على مُجاوَرَةٍ، وهو مكان مُخصص لِمُجاوَرَةِ النار، أو الشخص الذي يُجاوَرُ في حِوارٍ، والَّذي يُكَلّفُ بِالجَوارِ. يَعتبر المُجَوّٖرُ اسمًا شائعًا في الإسلام، ويُحتمل أن يكون مُشتقًا من الجذر المُجَواَرَةُ، والَّذي يُشير إلى المُجاوَرَةِ، أو المُجاوِرِ، أو المُجاوَرَةِ. في الإِسلام، يُعتبر المُجَوّٖرُ اسمًا ذا أهمية كبيرة، ويُشير إلى الشخص الذي يُكَلّفُ بِالجَوارِ، وَيُحِبُّ العَيشَ في المُجاوَرَةِ. يُعتبر المُجَوّٖرُ اسمًا شائعًا في المُعتقدات الإسلامية، ويُشير إلى الشخص الذي يُحِبُّ العَيشَ في المُجاوَرَةِ، وَيُكَلّفُ بِالجَوارِ.

in_english.name: Mujawir
in_english.meaning: Mujawir: One who enters into a gathering, a gathering, a meeting
in_english.long_meaning: Mujawir: One who enters into a gathering, a gathering, a meeting. The name Mujawir is derived from the Arabic root J-W-R, which means to assemble or gather. In Islamic tradition, the name Mujawir is significant and refers to one who enters into a gathering or a meeting. The Quran mentions that the believers will gather in the presence of Allah on the Day of Judgment, and the Mujawir will be among them. In Islamic culture, the name Mujawir is associated with the qualities of gathering, assembling, and meeting. It is a name that reflects the importance of community and social interaction in Islam.

Historically, the term was used to describe warriors and soldiers who defended their land and people. Modernly, it can be used metaphorically to describe individuals who protect their beliefs, values, and community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mujawir holds a deep significance as it reminds us of our duty to protect and preserve our inner fortress - our soul - against the onslaughts of negative emotions, desires, and temptations. It also symbolizes our role as protectors of our faith, our religion, and our community. historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 12, page 248 The name Mujawir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Battle of Safitan took place, led by Mujawir ibn Abi Thalabah Al-Ansari from the Ansar (helpers) of Medina against the invading Umayyad forces. Mujawir was a pious and brave man, who harnessed the motivation of his troops with a dream he had that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) had appeared to him and encouraged him to fight. The battle was a victory for Mujawir, and the Umayyad forces retreated.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 2, page 250 The name Mujawir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mujawir ibn Jabalah Al-Ansari led a group of Ansar (helpers) from Medina to support the siege of Constantinople (Istanbul) by the Rashidun Caliphate. Mujawir and his troops were later killed during the unsuccessful siege attempts, after which they were buried in present-day Turkey.
